description: The lint rules of FrameTrail-Conversational-UI: checks of a hypervideo that its schemas cannot express, run after changes (the editor's chat panel, MCP receipts, the command-line tool). Both interpreters implement every rule (client/lint/, server/lib/lint.php) with the same ids, severities and messages; shared/fixtures/lint/ holds them to it. $defs/result is what a lint gives back, in FrameTrail's schema subset.

rules.description: An overlay, annotation, code snippet or chapter that the player never reaches: it starts at or after the end of the video, or it lies before the video's start (its clip's in point). Without a known end only the start is checked.
An overlay or annotation that runs past the end of the video or begins before its start: the part outside is never shown.

Two overlays cover the same area at the same time, by their boxes (with box motion: the area they move in). Hotspots and cursors are left out: they are meant to lie over other overlays. Reported on the later of the two in stored order, with the other as related.

The clip or an item names a resource (resourceId, frametrail:resourceId) that is not in the resources index. An item keeps a copy of the resource it was made from, so it still shows; a clip that names its video only by the resource has no video. Checked only where the resources are known.

An overlay, annotation or code snippet lacks what its type needs: a source (embedded media, pages, files), text (text: text or title), HTML (html), a question and answers (quiz; answers for multipleChoice and multiSelect, each with text), a position (location: lat and lon), data (chart), the target of a hotspot's action, code (code snippet).
An overlay made from a library resource (frametrail:resourceId) or showing a media file (image, video, audio, pdf) has no license type (body frametrail:licenseType).
The chapters are not stored in order of their start, or two start at the same time. FrameTrail keeps them sorted, each start once; a file edited by hand may not.

Subtitle cues start at or after the end of the video: the subtitles may belong to another video. Reported once per language. Checked only for a clip without an out point (a trimmed video's subtitles go on after the out point).

errors.description: How many findings have the severity error.

warnings.description: How many findings have the severity warning.

findings.description: By rule, in the order of rules; within a rule as the items are listed.

kind.description: What it is about: a kind of item, the subtitles, or the hypervideo itself.

ref.description: Which one: an item's created, a chapter's start, the subtitles' language. Missing for the hypervideo.

creator.description: Annotations: the id of their creator (get_item takes it as creator).

message.description: What is wrong, in a sentence, for a person or a model.
